title: UN Security Council Unanimously Renews UNAMA Mandate for One Year (Resolution 2822)
detail: The UN Security Council voted unanimously (15-0) to adopt Resolution 2822 (2026), renewing the UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan's (UNAMA) mandate for a full year through June 17, 2027 — narrowly beating the expiry of the three-month technical rollover (Resolution 2818) adopted in March. Rather than a simple rollover, the mandate was modified: 'gender equality' language was replaced with 'equality for all women and girls,' climate-related language was reframed around disaster and water-scarcity impacts, and the Council requested a strategic review of the mission by March 31, 2027 plus quarterly implementation reporting. China, as penholder, navigated difficult negotiations balancing a US push to streamline the mission against Russian objections — with Russia's new Military-Technical Cooperation Agreement with the Taliban adding a fresh diplomatic variable to Moscow's council position.
